title: Rooftops to Load Curves: building-level electricity demand for Rwanda
crs: EPSG:4326 (lon, lat); metrics computed in EPSG:32735
time: local time, UTC+2; hours 0-23 are hour-starting bins
nulls: null means not observed or not modelled, never zero

cooling.rule: tmax_p95 (95th percentile of daily maximum 2 m temperature, 2020-2025) < 26 C: low; 26-29 C: medium; >= 29 C: high

peak_load.name: Estimated Peak Load
peak_load.definition: Expected coincident peak: the highest hourly mean of the building's expected load (sum over profiles of weight x hourly profile). Area peaks sum the hourly curves first, so they are smaller than the sum of building peaks.

annual_energy.name: Annual Energy Consumption
annual_energy.definition: Sum over profiles of weight x simulated daily kWh x 365. Potential demand if grid-connected, at 2022 appliance ownership. p10-p90 = day-to-day range.

cooling.name: Cooling Demand Category
cooling.definition: From the building's H3 r7 climate cell: tmax_p95 < 26 C Low, 26-29 C Medium, >= 29 C High. Relative indicator; AC demand is marginal in most of Rwanda.

load_profile.name: Load Profile Characteristics
load_profile.definition: From the 24-hour curve: peak hour, load factor (mean / peak), evening share (18:00-23:00), daytime share (08:00-17:00), night base (00:00-05:00 mean), weekday/weekend energy ratio, shape label.

pu_viability.name: Productive-Use Viability
pu_viability.definition: Candidate score: weighted mix of market access, customers nearby, grid proximity, ability to pay, agricultural context and building size, with weights for town trades or mills (formulas in meta.productive_use). Productive-use demand itself sits on tagged buildings plus an unlocated amount per area.

buildings.note: 6,434,247 footprints, all six national tables pass QA

heights.note: Google 2.5D Temporal; first-seen year is experimental

climate.note: ERA5-Land hourly from the Copernicus Climate Data Store, 2020-2025: temperature, humidity, rainfall, solar, monthly climatology

climate_cds.note: 1991-2020 baseline (daily statistics) still queued at Copernicus

labels.note: three deep-dive sectors (Muhoza partly) and a national sample; ~40% agreement with human labels, which are themselves uncertain (the imagery shows little beyond vegetation and roof shape)

profiles.note: 17 RAMP archetypes, assumptions signed off by the owner on 2026-10-12

demand_deep_dives.note: potential demand if grid-connected; class probabilities under 0.10 ignored (2026-10-12); productive use from tags + census

seasonal_profiles.note: monthly climate is now in; profiles are not yet seasonal

pu_viability.note: tagged buildings + unlocated census amount per area; candidate buildings ranked by criteria

grid_connection.note: classical model of household grid connection (DHS 2025 clusters); not yet applied to demand

market_access.label: Market access
market_access.formula: 0.5 x min(POIs within 250 m / 10, 1) + 0.5 x (1 - min(distance to major road / 2000 m, 1))

demand_density.label: Customers nearby
demand_density.formula: log10(1 + population density per km2) / log10(1 + 15000), capped at 1

grid_proximity.label: Grid proximity
grid_proximity.formula: 1 - min(distance to predicted MV line / 5000 m, 1)

agri_context.label: Agricultural context
agri_context.formula: cropland share (ESA WorldCover 2021) in the building's H3 r8 cell and its 6 neighbours (~1.5 km)

reported.label: Reported for the area
reported.note: published at area level by a source (here: NISR Establishment Census 2023, by district)

building_sum.label: Sum over buildings
building_sum.note: added up from individual buildings (modelled demand, tagged productive-use buildings)

unlocated.label: Unlocated, area only
unlocated.note: census productive use not tied to any building: an extra amount for the area, never a building's

trade_mix.why: The census does not split manufacturing by trade. Owner's rule: mills only in rural, roadside settings; tailors, welders and carpenters in towns. Equal shares among the town trades until a source says otherwise.

deep_dives.description: Dense mixed-use urban sector in Kigali, with shop-houses and informal areas.
Secondary city at ~1,850 m: cool, with a mixed commercial and residential core.
Warm eastern lowland (~1,350 m): rural, with a solar irrigation scheme (productive use).
